title: Earth Day & Looking After Our Planet
strapline: One small planet, and it's ours to look after — every little bit helps.
intent: Marking Earth Day helps children feel they belong to a wider world worth caring for and protecting.
Real acts of care — recycling, saving water, tending plants, picking up litter — build responsibility and habits that last.
Exploring nature, growing things and living creatures grows knowledge of and love for the living world.
Talking about looking after the planet gives children a sense that their small actions matter.
The theme turns caring for the earth into hands-on, hopeful, doable play.
implementation: Set up real caring tasks — a recycling sort, a plant to tend, a litter-pick of the garden, a water-saving job — that children can actually do.
Wonder together: 'What does our planet give us? How can we look after it?'
Get outside — explore nature, plant something, notice the creatures and plants that share our patch.
Feed in the message hopefully, never fearfully: 'Every little thing we do to help really matters.'
Link it to everyday habits — turning off taps, sorting the recycling, not wasting food — so care becomes routine.
Follow the children — some will sort and recycle all day, others will plant, dig and hunt for minibeasts.
key_questions: How can we look after our planet?
Where does this rubbish go — could we recycle it instead?
What do plants and creatures need from us?
What could we do to save water today?
What do you love most about being outside in nature?

impact.text: Children take part in real acts of caring for the planet — recycling, tending, saving.
Children treat living things gently and help them thrive.
Children explore nature and talk about what they find.
Children understand that their small actions help look after the world.
Children ask real questions about the planet and the living world.

enhancements: A recycling-sorting station with clean packaging to sort into the right bins.
A planting and tending patch to care for over time.
A garden litter-pick with gloves, bags and litter-pickers.
A minibeast and nature hunt to notice the living things around us.
A 'ways we look after our planet' display of the children's real actions.

playing_exploring: Children explore nature and get hands-on with caring for the world.
They sort, plant, dig and hunt with genuine engagement.
active_learning: Children keep up caring habits and tend living things over time.
They see planet-caring tasks through to the end.
creating_thinking: Children reason about where rubbish goes and how to waste less.
They grasp that their small actions add up and matter.
